City council approves new night bus routes

The city council voted on Tuesday to add four night bus routes connecting the
central station with the eastern suburbs. The routes will start in March and
run every 30 minutes between midnight and 5 a.m.

Council members said the decision followed a survey in which more than 6,000
residents asked for late-night transport after the closure of two suburban
rail stations for repairs. The transport department estimates the service will
cost 2.4 million a year, funded partly by a parking levy.

Local business owners welcomed the plan. "Our staff finish late and many of
them cannot afford taxis," said the owner of a restaurant near the station.
Opposition members questioned whether demand would last once the rail
stations reopen next year, and asked for a review after twelve months.

The council also approved new cycle lanes along the river road and agreed to
repaint pedestrian crossings near three primary schools before the new term.
